neighbours.label: political news context: the clause after a politician, critic or accusation ('a longtime critic of X,', 'amid accusations', 'allowed PM X to burnish')
fire: The minister, a vocal critic of the coal industry, said the plant should close.
The president was impeached last year amid allegations of bribery.
The treaty allowed the chancellor to strengthen her standing with conservative voters.
The mayor, a longtime opponent of the stadium deal, accused the council of secrecy.
The general seized power in a coup, amid claims of electoral fraud.
The prime minister's remarks on Friday drew a sharp rebuke from the opposition.
Authorities arrested lawyers, dissidents and bloggers, many of whom the regime called traitors.
The congresswoman, a frequent critic of the administration, called the policy illegal.
quiet: The chef, a vocal fan of local cheese, said the menu should change.
The bakery was closed last year amid a shortage of flour.
The new shoes allowed the runner to improve her time in the marathon.
The coach, a longtime fan of the old stadium, praised the groundskeepers.
The concert was moved indoors, amid fears of a thunderstorm.
The librarian's remarks on Friday drew laughter from the children.
The museum hired painters, carpenters and electricians, many of whom had worked there before.
The novelist, a frequent visitor to the island, described its beaches in detail.

notes: Probe: political sentences 0.30-0.72 ('critic of wind energy,' 0.72, 'amid accusations' 0.60, 'Abe to burnish his credentials' 0.57, 'senator, a fierce opponent,' 0.46). The same syntax in non-political text stayed low ('amid heavy rain' 0.075, 'allowed the young chef to' 0.05). So it is a topic or context, not the bare words 'amid' or ','.
